Is your website ready for AI search? A plain-English check

People now ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers which business to hire. Those tools can only recommend you if they can reach, read and trust your site. Here's how that works, what helps, and a quick check you can run today.

// key_takeaways

  • AI search tools still start with the basics: they need to reach your pages, read the text and understand who you are.
  • Allow the search crawlers you want, keep key facts in plain HTML, and describe your business with schema markup.
  • llms.txt is cheap to add, but no major AI search engine has said it relies on it. Don't buy it as a magic fix.

How AI search finds your business#

When someone asks ChatGPT for a reliable home care agency nearby, or asks Perplexity to compare Shopify developers, the tool doesn't guess. It searches the web, reads a handful of pages and writes an answer that quotes or links the sources it trusted.

So the question is the one SEO has always asked, with higher stakes: can these tools reach your site, read it and understand what you do? If the answer is no, you're not on the shortlist, and you never see the search that skipped you.

  1. 01

    Reach

    A crawler has to be allowed in. Your robots.txt file, security plugin or CDN decides that.

  2. 02

    Read

    It reads the text on the page. Many AI crawlers don't run JavaScript, so content that only appears after scripts load can be invisible to them.

  3. 03

    Understand

    Clear headings, direct answers and schema markup tell it what the page is about and who the business is.

  4. 04

    Trust

    Matching details across your site, Google Business Profile and directories, plus proof like case studies and reviews, make you safe to recommend.

Which crawlers matter#

Each AI company runs its own bots, and most separate the one that trains models from the one that fetches pages for answers. Blocking a training bot is a fair business choice. Blocking a search bot means you can't be cited.

  • OpenAI: OAI-SearchBot powers ChatGPT search results, GPTBot collects training data, and ChatGPT-User fetches a page when a user asks about it.
  • Anthropic: Claude-SearchBot for search, ClaudeBot for training and Claude-User for user requests.
  • Perplexity: PerplexityBot builds its index and Perplexity-User handles live lookups.
  • Google: AI Overviews and AI Mode use the normal Googlebot. The separate Google-Extended setting covers Gemini, not your place in Google Search.
  • Microsoft: Copilot answers lean on the Bing index, so Bingbot access and Bing Webmaster Tools still count.
// check this first

Some security plugins and CDNs block AI crawlers by default. If your site sits behind one, look at its bot settings before anything else. One blocking rule can cancel out every other fix on this list.

What helps AI tools read and trust your site#

  • Put the answer near the top. Say what you do, for whom and where in the first lines of the page. AI answers favour pages that state facts plainly.
  • Keep key facts in the HTML. Services, prices, locations and contact details should be real text, not baked into images or loaded by a script after the page appears.
  • Use schema markup. Organization or LocalBusiness, Service, Product and FAQ schema describe your business in a format machines read without guessing.
  • Give each service its own page. One page listing everything you do gives an AI tool nothing specific to quote. A focused page per service does, which is why this site has a separate page for each service.
  • Make your details match everywhere. Business name, address, phone number and hours should agree across your site, Google Business Profile and directories.
  • Show proof. Case studies, reviews and named clients give an answer engine a reason to pick you over a competitor making the same claims.

What about llms.txt?#

llms.txt is a plain text file at the root of your site that sums up who you are and links your most important pages, written for AI tools. It's a proposal, not a standard. Google has said it doesn't use it, and the other big AI search engines haven't confirmed that they read it.

I still add one for most clients. It takes an hour, costs nothing to serve, and forces a useful exercise: writing down in plain words what the business does and which pages matter. I've done this for The Walker Group and Graceful Connections Home Care. Just don't treat it as the fix. Crawler access, readable content and schema do the heavy lifting.

Questions, answered#

Will this get me into ChatGPT answers?

Nobody can promise a place in an AI answer, the same way nobody can promise a Google ranking. What you can do is remove the reasons to skip you. That part is technical, and it's fixable.

How long does an AI search check take?

For most small business sites, the check and the quick fixes (crawler settings, schema, llms.txt and a few content changes) take 1 to 3 days.

Do I need to rewrite my whole site?

Rarely. Most of the work is structure: clearer headings, a short summary at the top of key pages, schema and one page per service. Your existing copy usually stays.
